literal: In their heart me banishing those who did, do they not feel shame, in my heart unceasingly coming?
translation: Are they not ashamed, those who have barred me from their own heart, to keep coming unceasingly into mine?
modern: தம்முடைய நெஞ்சத்தில் என்னை வரவிடாமல் தடுத்துக்கொண்டவர், என்னுடைய நெஞ்சத்தில் இடைவிடாமல் வந்து கொண்டிருப்பதற்கு வெட்கப்பட மாட்டாரா?
explanation: The heroine, suffering in separation, speaks of her beloved who has left her. She notes that he has locked her out of his own thoughts and heart, yet he constantly and unceasingly enters her heart as a persistent memory. She wonders, with a touch of irony, if he feels no shame in intruding so relentlessly into her mind while denying her a place in his. The contrast between 'their heart' and 'my heart' highlights the painful asymmetry of their love during separation.
